clue.text: Substitute taking part in practice sessions, perhaps

definitions.text: Substitute taking part in practice sessions, perhaps

parts.words: Substitute taking part in practice sessions, perhaps
parts.note: reads like a reserve player turning out for training, but the practice is a doctor's surgery and the sessions are its consulting hours, covered by a stand-in doctor

explanation.surface: A reserve player gets a run-out in the team's training sessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Practice sessions' suggests sport; in fact a medical practice holds surgery sessions, and the stand-in doctor who covers them is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor or cleric who deputises for a colleague temporarily is known by this Latin-derived term.

clue.text: In a pub one understands point of dealing with organisation

indicators.note: In tells us the following pieces are placed inside the pub word

parts.note: a local is your nearby pub

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece standing under another is written below it, so the point comes first and the one goes beneath

parts.note: the gist is the main point
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: In a pub, someone grasps the key point about how things are organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'understands' is read as 'under-stands': in a down clue the one is written beneath the point, and that pair goes into the pub word, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Logistics is the business of planning and organising supplies and operations, so the adjective describes that kind of arrangement.

clue.text: Raised police dog

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word writes it from the bottom upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: the RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, the former police force of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A police dog is lifted up off the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A cur is a mongrel or ill-bred dog.

clue.text: Swarmed around, gathering litter

parts.note: a mob is a crowd, a gathering of people
litter is straw bedding for animals, so a bed

explanation.surface: People crowded round as someone collected rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mobbed is to have a crowd press round you, as a celebrity is besieged by fans.

clue.text: Receives first part of television broadcast yielding little information

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order
first part of points to the opening letter of the word television

explanation.surface: Someone picks up the start of a TV transmission that tells them very little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like part of the television picture but rearranges RECEIVES plus T, the first letter of 'television'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone close-mouthed who keeps things hidden gives little away.

clue.text: Tinker goes round like mischievous child, greedily

indicators.note: goes round says the tinker's name surrounds the next piece

parts.note: Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in the induction to Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew
elfish means impish, like a naughty little sprite

explanation.surface: A naughty child is a little tinker who grabs things for themself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinker' suggests a scamp, but it is Christopher Sly, the drunken tinker in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting only for one's own gain, without regard for others, is how a greedy person behaves.

clue.text: Stick to cold fish

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
the ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay with cold fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling is to adhere tightly, like a limpet to a rock.

clue.text: Fabulous place where the Spanish artist gets into parties

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the

indicators.note: gets into says the artist is placed inside the parties

parts.note: a do is a party, so two of them make parties
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A Spanish painter turns up at every party in some legendary spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary city of gold sought by conquistadors is a byword for an imaginary land of riches.

clue.text: In the cooler, hear fellow soldier

parts.note: a fan is a device that cools the air
to hear a case in court is to try it
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: In prison, word reaches a fellow soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cooler' looks like slang for prison but is a fan; 'hear' is what a judge does to a case, TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot soldier serving in the infantry.

clue.text: Nobleman associated with court in London

definitions.text: Nobleman associated with court in London

parts.words: Nobleman associated with court in London
parts.note: a peer who might attend the royal court, but the court is the London district named after such a peer, home to a famous exhibition centre

explanation.surface: A peer with connections at a London court.
explanation.walkthrough: Earls Court is a district of west London; the clue suggests a royal or law court instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A British peer ranking above a viscount and below a marquess.

clue.text: Soldier eating a coarse biscuit

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so the soldier surrounds what follows

parts.note: GI is a US soldier
ribald means coarse, vulgar humour

explanation.surface: A soldier munches a rough biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' looks like the definition (Garibaldi was a soldier) but gives GI; the biscuit is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat currant-filled biscuit named after the Italian patriot, known in Britain as a 'squashed fly' biscuit.

clue.text: Give way to delay

definitions.meaning: to yield or submit to someone's judgement

explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers both deferring to a superior and deferring a payment.

clue.text: It gives one a hot tip for joining golf club after one leaves army service

definitions.text: It gives one a hot tip for joining

indicators.note: after places the club at the end, following the trimmed service word
one leaves means the letter for one departs from the service word

parts.note: soldiering is serving in the army
I is the Roman numeral for one
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: Someone takes up golf after leaving the army and gets a hot tip.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hot tip' sounds like insider advice; it is the heated point of a joining tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool with a heated point used to melt metal alloy to join wires and components.

clue.text: Member of military force cracking up in alien region

indicators.note: cracking up suggests breaking into pieces, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A soldier has a breakdown in a strange land.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier of the French Foreign Legion, or of a Roman legion.

clue.text: Repugnance of overdrawn head receiving reminders of debt

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the debt reminders go inside

parts.note: OD is the bank abbreviation for overdrawn
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness
IOUs are notes acknowledging money owed

explanation.surface: A head who is overdrawn hates getting IOUs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overdrawn head' reads as one person in debt; it splits into two pieces, with the debt reminders between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The quality of being hateful or offensive, which provokes disgust.

clue.text: Ancient island with a resort

parts.note: a resort is something tried as a recourse, a go or attempt

explanation.surface: An old island that has a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient' is an old word for an ensign: Iago is Othello's ancient in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: In Othello the scheming ensign is called the general's ancient, an old military rank.

clue.text: Pushed for university in more ancient setting in Slough

indicators.note: setting in means the built-up piece is set inside the slough word

parts.note: to slough is to cast off, as a snake sheds its skin

indicators.note: in places the university letter inside the older word

parts.note: older means more ancient

explanation.surface: Someone shoved their way to a place at an older university in Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, but here it is the verb 'shed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder someone aside is to push or jostle them.

clue.text: It's unpleasant when ugly hints are spread abroad

indicators.note: spread abroad means scattered about, so the letters are dispersed into a new order

explanation.surface: Nasty rumours spread about someone are unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something displeasing to the eye is ugly to look at.

clue.text: Pot or container on top of broken basin

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top of puts the container above the broken basin

parts.note: a can is a container

indicators.note: broken says the letters of basin are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A pot or jar sits on a broken basin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' looks like a container, but here it is slang for the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot is slang for marijuana.

clue.text: Version of holy book revised in Leo's papacy

indicators.note: revised means altered and rewritten, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new version of the Bible was produced while Leo was pope.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic versions of the Bible name the book of Revelation with this Greek title.

clue.text: Charges resulting when sides of bacon go missing

indicators.note: sides of refers to the outer letters of the word for bacon
go missing means those outer letters are dropped

parts.note: gammon is cured ham or bacon from the hind leg

explanation.surface: When the bacon disappears, accusations follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sides of bacon' looks like the meat itself; it means the first and last letters of GAMMON, which go missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Charges of explosive or shot are ammunition, informally shortened.

clue.text: Block the path of some dim pedestrian

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A slow-witted walker gets in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To obstruct or hinder progress.

clue.text: Neutral states

parts.note: reads as countries taking no side, but the states are conditions of being uncommitted to any bloc

explanation.definitionFit: A neutral country refuses to join any bloc or alliance, and that refusal is its political stance.

clue.text: Started to smoke, being soaked

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers lighting a cigarette and, as slang, being drunk.

clue.text: Wordless sort of singer brooded about note

indicators.note: about means around, so the brooding word goes round the note

parts.note: a hen that brooded sat on its eggs
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: A singer who doesn't use words sat moping over a note.
explanation.definitionFit: Jazz singing in nonsense syllables rather than words is given this name, so a singer of that style is described by it.

clue.text: Rise in region reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a clime is a region, especially one known by its climate

explanation.surface: An increase in a region is reported.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend or go up.

clue.text: Claim by Windsor mistress at beginning of book

parts.note: a title is a right or claim to something, as a title to property
Mistress Page is one of the Merry Wives of Windsor in Shakespeare's comedy

explanation.surface: A royal mistress makes a claim at the start of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windsor mistress' hints at a royal lover; it is Mistress Page from Shakespeare's The Merry Wives of Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: The leaf at the front of a book that bears its name and author.

clue.text: A silence in the wood

parts.note: sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A hush falls in the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardwood tree whose timber is used for tool handles and sports equipment.

clue.text: Extremely holy man's work at start of religious system

indicators.note: at start of places the man's work before the last piece

parts.note: Theo is a man's name, so the man's is Theo's
op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so the first and last letters of holy

explanation.surface: A very holy man's work begins a religious system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely holy' suggests great piety; it gives the first and last letters of 'holy', and 'at start of' puts the man's work in front of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A mystical philosophy claiming direct knowledge of the divine, as in Madame Blavatsky's movement.

clue.text: Characteristic spirit of Englishman when made to look small
